phases.note: FROM PHASE 6 (landed b4bc490), with one correction the coordinator verified. (a) MEASURED: 14 nina_turns image jobs have an args.replyToId resolving to nothing; reported by nina:memory-reap, never deleted (invariant 9). So planJobJump's 'gone' arm and its NINA_JOB_JUMP_NOTE copy are LIVE on real rows -- build and test them as the common case. (b) Phase 6 called this 'larger than the plan guessed'; it withdrew that itself. Its count is dangling args.replyToId; the plan's 15 is rows carrying error_code='dispatched'. Different predicates, possibly non-overlapping, and 14 < 15. Not a scope increase. (c) REJECT phase 6's advice to treat 'the triggering message is gone' and 'the session was removed' as ONE state. It proved the converse of what that needs: the cascade means no message survives a deleted session, but collapsing the states requires that no message is GONE while its session SURVIVES -- and deleteNinaMessage does exactly that. It is unchanged by phase 6 (deliberately, per lib/db/schema.ts:857 which phase 6 itself wrote) and is reachable in production from lib/admin/chatPhotoActions.ts:231 and :283, the /admin chat-photo delete path. Collapsing them would tell a runner 'the session was removed' about a job whose session is alive and whose single message they deleted through /admin. Keep the kinds distinct.

phases.note: PHASE 6. removeNinaSession is now a 4-statement db.batch: purge facts, purge slots (minus pending_promises), prune pending_promises per ENTRY, session delete LAST. Correlated subquery, not a pre-read. No FK, no migration; drizzle/ gained no file and db:check is clean. Two forks decided on the ladder: (1) drizzle exists() emits no parens around a raw sql template -- the plan's Step 1 asserts the opposite outright -- producing 'and exists select 1 from', a syntax error; hand-parenthesised the template rather than relax the test, rung 2 (exit criteria need the purge to EXECUTE). (2) the no-FK comment named lib/admin/memoryStore.ts in full and tripped admin.memory.test.ts's textual guard over lib/nina; rephrased the comment, guard stands. Reap APPLIED after full-table \copy snapshot at /home/miftah/nina-memory-snapshot-20260906/{facts,slots}-backup.csv (13 facts, 6 slots dumped whole, not orphans-only): deleted 1 fact, 1 slot (nickname 'tah', the plan's named accepted cost), pruned 1 promise list 2->1; second consecutive dry run reports ZERO. The dry run is also the only thing that proves the hand-written jsonb_array_elements/with-ordinality/jsonb_agg expression is ACCEPTED BY POSTGRES -- the unit suite asserts that SQL as a string, which proves the string and not the parse. FOR PHASE 4: 14 nina_turns image jobs have an args.replyToId that resolves to nothing; reported, never deleted (invariant 9). CORRECTION to my first note: I called that 'larger than the plan guessed' and that was wrong -- the plan's 15 counts rows with error_code='dispatched', a DIFFERENT predicate, so the two sets are not comparable and may not overlap. The usable finding is only that the 'gone' path is a common case rather than hypothetical; phase 4's planJobJump already handles it and needs no redesign. 2698 tests / 142 files green, six guards pass, typecheck clean, lint 0 errors. Committed by explicit pathspec; phase 1's four in-flight files left untouched.
